Well, if we were just to mention some of the main ones, we could point first to the three of— 1) A foundation consciousness which was not such that to be it was automatically to be the group of six different types of consciousness; 2) A unique way of denying apperception; and 3) The denial that one can—with the “independent” form of reasoning—inspire the view of the way things really are, in the mind of an opponent.

29183.acip: SHES PA KHAS LEN PA BZHIN DU PHYI ROL GYI DON YANG KHAS BLANG DGOS PA DANG, NYAN RANG LA DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN MED PAR RTOGS PA YOD PA DANG, CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN NYON MONGS SU 'JOG PA DANG, ZHIG PA DNGOS PO YIN PA DANG, DE'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS DUS GSUM GYI 'JOG TSUL THUN MONG MA YIN PA SOGS YIN NO,,
29183.wylie: shes pa khas len pa bzhin du phyi rol gyi don yang khas blang dgos pa dang, nyan rang la dngos po rang bzhin med par rtogs pa yod pa dang, chos kyi bdag 'dzin nyon mongs su 'jog pa dang, zhig pa dngos po yin pa dang, de'i rgyu mtshan gyis dus gsum gyi 'jog tshul thun mong ma yin pa sogs yin no
29183.english: And then there are also: 4) The fact that—just as one accepts awareness—you must also accept the existence of outside objects. 5) The idea that listeners and self-made buddhas do realize the fact that things have no nature of their own. 6) The determination that the tendency to grasp to a self-existence of things is a negative emotion. 7) The idea that the fact of something having ended is itself a functioning thing. 8) The concept that—due to that being the case—the three times can be defined in a unique way.

29250.acip: LUGS 'DI'I GANG ZAG GI 'JOG TSUL THUN MONG MA YIN PA SHES NA NAM MKHA' DANG RNAM SHES MTHA' YAS DANG CI YANG MED PA GSUM DU SKYES PA'I 'PHAGS PA'I RGYUD LA, 'JIG RTEN LAS 'DAS PA ZAG MED KYI SEMS MNGON DU GYUR PA NA, 'JIG RTEN PA'I SEMS GZHAN MED PAS DE RNAMS KYI 'GRO BA LDOG PAR 'GYUR RO, ZHES PA DANG,
29250.wylie: lugs 'di'i gang zag gi 'jog tshul thun mong ma yin pa shes na nam mkha' dang rnam shes mtha' yas dang ci yang med pa gsum du skyes pa'i 'phags pa'i rgyud la, 'jig rten las 'das pa zag med kyi sems mngon du gyur pa na, 'jig rten pa'i sems gzhan med pas de rnams kyi 'gro ba ldog par 'gyur ro, zhes pa dang
29250.english: If we can come to an understanding of the unique manner in which this particular system posits the person, then it would appear that our position could no longer be challenged by arguments such as the following. The first here would be where someone asks us to consider the mind stream of a realized being who has taken birth into one of the three levels of Limitless Space; Limitless Awareness; or Nothing At All. When a state of mind which transcends the normal world—an unstained state of mind—manifests itself, then since there can be no other, worldly states of mind, their functioning is said to be suspended.

29339.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I KUN GZHI KHAS LEN NA KUN GZHI'I BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LAS GZUGS SGRA SOGS SU SNANG BA TZAM DU ZAD KYI, PHYI ROL GYI DON MED PAR KHAS BLANG DGOS NA, DE NYID LAS,
29339.wylie: de 'dra ba'i kun gzhi khas len na kun gzhi'i bag chags smin pa las gzugs sgra sogs su snang ba tsam du zad kyi, phyi rol gyi don med par khas blang dgos na, de nyid las
29339.english: If we were to accept a foundation consciousness like the one you have described, then we would have to agree to the idea that there exist no outer objects; we would have to say that things like visible form, and sounds, were nothing but phantoms appearing out of the ripening of deep seeds inside of foundation consciousness. And then it would be as the same work describes it:

29375.acip: GANG GI PHYIR BYANG SEMS 'DIS NANG GI BAG CHAGS SMIN PA LAS GZUGS SOGS 'BYUNG BAR 'CHAD PAR 'GYUR BA'I RIGS PAS SEMS LA RANG LAS RDZAS GZHAN GYI GZUNG BA MED PAR DE LAS DON GZHAN PA'I DE 'DZIN PAR BYED PA MA MTHONG ZHING, SRID PA KHAMS GSUM PO NI RNAM PAR SHES PA TZAM MO ZHES RAB TU RTOGS PAS TE NAS,
29375.wylie: gang gi phyir byang sems 'dis nang gi bag chags smin pa las gzugs sogs 'byung bar 'chad par 'gyur ba'i rigs pas sems la rang las rdzas gzhan gyi gzung ba med par de las don gzhan pa'i de 'dzin par byed pa ma mthong zhing, srid pa khams gsum po ni rnam par shes pa tsam mo zhes rab tu rtogs pas te nas
29375.english: The bodhisattva utilizes reasoning—which we are about to explain—to understand how physical form and the like come into being through the ripening of deep seeds inside of themselves; which is to say, this logic allows them to understand how there are no objects of perception which are such that to be them is not to be the mind itself. They see no entities which act to hold to these objects and are separate from them. And so—which is to say, first—they come to a deep realization that all three realms of existence are only consciousness itself.

29392.acip: THUN MONG NI SNOD KYI 'JIG RTEN GYI SA BON GANG YIN PA'O, ,THUN MONG MA YIN PA DE NI SO SO RANG GI SKYE MCHED KYI SA BON GANG YIN PA'O, ,THUN MONG GANG YIN PA DE NI TSOR BA MED PA 'BYUNG BA'I SA BON NO,
29392.wylie: thun mong ni snod kyi 'jig rten gyi sa bon gang yin pa'o, ,thun mong ma yin pa de ni so so rang gi skye mched kyi sa bon gang yin pa'o, ,thun mong gang yin pa de ni tshor ba med pa 'byung ba'i sa bon no
29392.english: It is that thing which is the seed for the vessel of the world, that all of us share. It is that thing which is the seed for those things which are not shared: for the doors of sense of different individuals. It is the seed for those things which occur that are shared, but which do not exhibit sensation.

29983.acip: ,GAL TE 'DI DAG SEMS TZAM ZHES MKHYEN NAS, ,DE LAS GZUGS NYID DGAG PAR MDZAD NA NI, ,SLAR YANG DE LAS BDAG NYID CHEN POS SEMS, ,GTI MUG LAS LAS SKYES PAR CI PHYIR GSUNGS,
29983.wylie: gal te 'di dag sems tsam zhes mkhyen nas, ,de las gzugs nyid dgag par mdzad na ni, ,slar yang de las bdag nyid chen pos sems, ,gti mug las las skyes par ci phyir gsungs
29983.english: Suppose all these Were referred to As “only the mind,” And the Buddha Knew this, and so Meant in this To deny “form itself.” And then how Could it be in it For the Great Being To state that the mind Was born from Dark ignorance And karma?

30000.acip: DE LA RMA BYA LA SOGS PA'I MDONGS LA SOGS PA SNA TSOGS PA NI, SEMS CAN DE RNAMS KHO NA'I LAS THUN MONG MA YIN PAS SKYED PA'O,,
30000.wylie: de la rma bya la sogs pa'i mdongs la sogs pa sna tshogs pa ni, sems can de rnams kho na'i las thun mong ma yin pas skyed pa'o
30000.english: And so things like the extraordinary variety of colors found in things such as the feathers of the peacock are all objects which were created by the unique karma only of living beings themselves.

30032.acip: DES NA RNAM PAR SHES PA'I RKYEN GYIS MING GZUGS SKYE BA SOGS KHAS LEN KYANG PHYI ROL KHAS LEN MI DGOS PAR 'DOD PA LA BZLOG NAS SMRA BAR MI BYA STE, SEMS TZAM GYI THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I RNAM GZHAG STON PA NA DE LTAR BSHAD PA SHIN TU MANG NGO,,
30032.wylie: des na rnam par shes pa'i rkyen gyis ming gzugs skye ba sogs khas len kyang phyi rol khas len mi dgos par 'dod pa la bzlog nas smra bar mi bya ste, sems tsam gyi thun mong ma yin pa'i rnam gzhag ston pa na de ltar bshad pa shin tu mang ngo
30032.english: As such, I would encourage people not to say it all backwards here: don't go around claiming that you can accept for example that name & form arise through the factor of consciousness, but that this doesn't necessitate accepting things on the outside. We see a massive number of people offering this type of explanation when they make presentations of the unique beliefs of the Mind Only.

30075.acip: 'DI RNAMS LA GO BA MTHA' CHOD PAR MA CHAGS NA SPYIR DBU SEMS DANG KHYAD PAR DU LUGS 'DI'I GNAD THUN MONG MA YIN PA RNAMS MI SHES PAR MTHONG NAS DRANG NGES RNAM PAR 'BYED PAR ZHIB TU BSHAD DO,,
30075.wylie: 'di rnams la go ba mtha' chod par ma chags na spyir dbu sems dang khyad par du lugs 'di'i gnad thun mong ma yin pa rnams mi shes par mthong nas drang nges rnam par 'byed par zhib tu bshad do
30075.english: I have come to the realization that if a person fails to develop a definitive understanding of these points, then more generally they will never come to an understanding of the schools of the Middle Way and the Mind Only—most especially the unique, crucial points of this particular way of things. As such, I have explained covered all these ideas in great detail in my presentation on distinguishing the literal & the figurative.

30436.acip: JI LTAR GRANGS CAN DAG GIS BDAG KHAS BLANGS PA DE BZHIN DU, BDAG DE'I DBYE BA CUNG ZAD CUNG ZAD LA BRTEN NAS MU STEGS CAN RNAMS KYI LUGS NI THA DAD PAR 'GYUR TE,
30436.wylie: ji ltar grangs can dag gis bdag khas blangs pa de bzhin du, bdag de'i dbye ba cung zad cung zad la brten nas mu stegs can rnams kyi lugs ni tha dad par 'gyur te
30436.english: Thus then do those of the Numerist School accept the idea of a self; and based upon various minor distinctions in this presentation of a self, there have developed the different systems of the River Schools.

30592.acip: MDO GZHAN LAS GZUGS BDAG MIN NO ZHES SOGS KYIS GZUGS SOGS RNAMS BDAG YIN PA BKAG PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
30592.wylie: mdo gzhan las gzugs bdag min no zhes sogs kyis gzugs sogs rnams bdag yin pa bkag par gsungs pa'i phyir ro
30592.english: This is due to the fact that—in other sutras—the understanding was expressed that “form is not the self”; and so on. Which is to say, it was denied that form and the like could be the self.

30601.acip: MDO GANG LAS GZUGS SOGS RNAMS KYANG BDAG YIN PA BKAG PA DE LAS NI, BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA'I BDAG 'JIG LTA'I DMIGS PA 'DIS PHUNG PO LEN PA'I PHUNG PO'I NYE BAR LEN PA CAN RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA BKAG PAR RIG PAR BYA STE, GZUGS SOGS BDAG MIN PAR GSUNGS PA DE NI DE KHO NA NYID LA SEMS PA'I SKABS YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
30601.wylie: mdo gang las gzugs sogs rnams kyang bdag yin pa bkag pa de las ni, brten nas btags pa'i bdag 'jig lta'i dmigs pa 'dis phung po len pa'i phung po'i nye bar len pa can rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag par rig par bya ste, gzugs sogs bdag min par gsungs pa de ni de kho na nyid la sems pa'i skabs yin pa'i phyir ro
30601.english: There are other sutras in which it is also denied that form and the rest could be the self; and from this we should understand that the self as labeled in dependence—what it is that the view of destruction focuses upon—serves to deny the idea that the one it is that takes on the parts to the person as these parts are taken could exist through any nature of its own. That is, statements that form and the rest are not the self are made in the context of considering the topic of suchness.

30604.acip: BDAG PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA MING GI THA SNYAD KYI DBANG GIS BZHAG PA TZAM GYI GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED KYI 'JOG TSUL THUN MONG MA YIN PA,
30604.wylie: bdag phung po la brten nas btags pa ming gi tha snyad kyi dbang gis bzhag pa tsam gyi gang zag gi bdag med kyi 'jog tshul thun mong ma yin pa
30604.english: This method of describing the lack of a self to the person—where we describe the self as no more than something established through the power of terms, names labeled on the basis of the parts to the person—is truly unique.

30607.acip: SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYI DGONGS PA SHIN TU PHRA BA'I GNAS RNAMS RJEN CHER DU STON PA'I MKHAS PA'I DBANG PO'I BZHED PA THUN MONG MA YIN PA 'DI RNAMS LEGS PAR SHES PA LA 'BAD PAR GYIS SHIG
30607.wylie: sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das kyi dgongs pa shin tu phra ba'i gnas rnams rjen cher du ston pa'i mkhas pa'i dbang po'i bzhed pa thun mong ma yin pa 'di rnams legs par shes pa la 'bad par gyis shig
30607.english: Thus then are they lords among masters, who have taken this extremely subtle intent of the Buddha, the Conqueror, and laid it out completely bare for us. And so I beg you to make massive efforts to learn, deeply, the truly unique positions of these thinkers. Sutra never said the parts were the self

30659.acip: LTOS 'GRUB 'DI LA GNYIS KA PHAN TSUN LTOS PA'I THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I 'JOG LUGS YOD PA RNAMS SHES DGOS PAR YOD DO,,
30659.wylie: ltos 'grub 'di la gnyis ka phan tshun ltos pa'i thun mong ma yin pa'i 'jog lugs yod pa rnams shes dgos par yod do
30659.english: And as regards this process of reliance, you should understand the unique methods in which we establish both of the two here as sharing a mutual reliance.

30843.acip: GSUNG RAB KYI DON DU 'GREL PA, THUB PA'I DGONGS PA THUN MONG MA YIN PA YIN PAS, RNAM DPYOD CAN GYIS DGONGS PA 'GREL LUGS 'DI LA SBYANG BAR BYA'O,,
30843.wylie: gsung rab kyi don du 'grel pa, thub pa'i dgongs pa thun mong ma yin pa yin pas, rnam dpyod can gyis dgongs pa 'grel lugs 'di la sbyang bar bya'o
30843.english: Taking this as the meaning of scripture represents the perfectly unique intent of the Able Ones; as such, those of you possessed of discernment should verse yourselves in this manner of explaining their true thought. The actual point about eliminating extremes

31287.acip: DA NI SHER PHYIN LA LHAG PAR MOS PA'I BYANG SEMS KYI THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I YON TAN BRJOD PA'I SGO NAS, SHER PHYIN GYI SKABS RDZOGS PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR DU BSHAD PA,
31287.wylie: da ni sher phyin la lhag par mos pa'i byang sems kyi thun mong ma yin pa'i yon tan brjod pa'i sgo nas, sher phyin gyi skabs rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir du bshad pa
31287.english: And so we will now make an explanation with a view towards wrapping up our section on the perfection of wisdom, by describing the unique personal qualities of a bodhisattva who has a special longing for this wisdom perfection.

31518.acip: MI 'GAL TE BDEN GNYIS KYI MTSAN NYID SNGAR BSHAD PA NI SPYIR BTANG LA DGONGS LA, SANGS RGYAS KYI YE SHES KYI MKHYEN TSUL NI SA BCU PA MAN CHAD DANG, THUN MONG MA YIN PA DMIGS BSAL GYI DBANG DU BYAS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
31518.wylie: mi 'gal te bden gnyis kyi mtshan nyid sngar bshad pa ni spyir btang la dgongs la, sangs rgyas kyi ye shes kyi mkhyen tshul ni sa bcu pa man chad dang, thun mong ma yin pa dmigs bsal gyi dbang du byas pa yin pa'i phyir ro
31518.english: And yet in fact there is no contradiction here. The definition presented earlier for the two realities was meant only to be a general description; it was made only with reference to the way in which the high knowledge of a Buddha does its knowing at the tenth level on down; and so it was treating a special case, not something typical.

31779.acip: DES NA RANG GI LUGS 'DI SEMS TZAM PA DANG YANG THUN MONG MA YIN PAR MA ZAD, MGON PO KLU SGRUB DANG 'PHAGS PA LHA'I DGONGS PA 'GREL BA'I DBU MA PA GZHAN GYI LUGS DANG YANG THUN MONG MA YIN PAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG CES 'DOMS PA PO,,
31779.wylie: des na rang gi lugs 'di sems tsam pa dang yang thun mong ma yin par ma zad, mgon po klu sgrub dang 'phags pa lha'i dgongs pa 'grel ba'i dbu ma pa gzhan gyi lugs dang yang thun mong ma yin par shes par gyis shig ces 'doms pa po
31779.english: As such, what our author is actually advising us of here is the following— Not only should we say that the system that we ourselves are presenting here is nothing held in common even with those of the Mind Only. You must also understand the point that no one can say, either, that our beliefs are held in common with those of other systems of some thinkers of the Middle Way School who are attempting to comment upon the true intent of our Savior, Nagarjuna, and Aryadeva.

31781.acip: THA SNYAD DU YANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I STENG NAS, BDEN GNYIS KYI RNAM GZHAG MDZAD PA 'DI LA BRTEN NAS RANG RGYUD KYI GRUB MTHA' DANG, KUN GZHI MI BZHED PA SOGS KYI BSHAD SROL THUN MONG MA YIN PA MANG DU YOD PA NI, DRANG NGES RNAM 'BYED LA SOGS PAR RGYAS PAR BSHAD PAS 'DIR MA SMOS SO,,
31781.wylie: tha snyad du yang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa med pa'i steng nas, bden gnyis kyi rnam gzhag mdzad pa 'di la brten nas rang rgyud kyi grub mtha' dang, kun gzhi mi bzhed pa sogs kyi bshad srol thun mong ma yin pa mang du yod pa ni, drang nges rnam 'byed la sogs par rgyas par bshad pas 'dir ma smos so
31781.english: And so it is true that—even speaking nominally—there is nothing that could exist by definition. In addition, we have our presentation here of the two different types of reality. Based on this, there are many different, unique, systems of explanation—such as the school of the Independent Group, and those who do not accept the concept of a storehouse consciousness. I have explained all these at great length in works such as Distinguishing the Figurative from the Literal; as such, I will not go into them further here.

31784.acip: 'PHAGS PA'I DGONGS PA 'CHAD LUGS 'DI NI THUN MONG MA YIN PA YIN PA'I PHYIR, 'PHAGS PA'I THUGS DGONGS MI SHES SHING, GSUNG RAB KYI DE KHO NA NYID NGES PA MED PAR,
31784.wylie: 'phags pa'i dgongs pa 'chad lugs 'di ni thun mong ma yin pa yin pa'i phyir, 'phags pa'i thugs dgongs mi shes shing, gsung rab kyi de kho na nyid nges pa med par
31784.english: This way of explaining the true intent of The Arya is truly unique; as such, there have been people who rejected this teaching beyond the world; this was done by those who had not grasped the true and holy intent of The Arya, and who had not yet ascertained suchness as presented in the scriptures.

31886.acip: a4) BYANG SEMS KYI SBYIN PA'I PHAN YON THUN MONG MA YIN PA BSTAN PA, [v. I.13a]
31886.wylie: a4) byang sems kyi sbyin pa'i phan yon thun mong ma yin pa bstan pa, [v. i.13a]
31886.english: A description of the unique type of giving practiced by a bodhisattva

32005.acip: b14) NYON MONGS KYI RNAM GZHAG THUN MONG MA YIN PA BSHAD PA, [117a]
32005.wylie: b14) nyon mongs kyi rnam gzhag thun mong ma yin pa bshad pa, [117a]
32005.english: An explanation of this unique presentation of the negative emotions

32697.acip: SPRIN NI KLU SOGS KYI BSAM PA'I DBANG GIS MKHA' LA SKYE ZHING 'JIG PA LTAR 'DUS BYAS RNAMS NI, THUN MONG DANG THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I LAS DBANG GIS SKYE 'JIG BYED BAR 'GYUR ZHES PA'I DPE RNAMS KYIS KYANG 'DUS BYAS THAMS CAD BDEN MED DU BSHAD DO,,
32697.wylie: sprin ni klu sogs kyi bsam pa'i dbang gis mkha' la skye zhing 'jig pa ltar 'dus byas rnams ni, thun mong dang thun mong ma yin pa'i las dbang gis skye 'jig byed bar 'gyur zhes pa'i dpe rnams kyis kyang 'dus byas thams cad bden med du bshad do
32697.english: Clouds are something that gather and fade in the sky, depending on the wishes of the dragons and such. Things brought about by causes are the same; depending on the influence of karma which is either communal or not, they rise or die out. Each of the metaphors above is also meant to represent how no object brought about by causes has any true existence.

32983.acip: YANG DE NYID LAS, LUGS DAM PA 'DIS NI YAN LAG TSOGS PA TZAM DANG DE'I YA GYAL SOGS GANG YANG YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA'I MTSAN GZHIR MI RUNG YANG, YAN LAG CAN LA SOGS PA MING DU BTAGS PA TZAM LA BYA BYED LEGS PAR 'JOG NUS PA GSUNG RAB KYI DON DU 'GREL BA THUB PA'I DGONGS PA THUN MONG MA YIN PA YIN PAS DGONGS PA 'GREL LUGS 'DI LA SBYANG BAR BYA'O, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR YIN PAS SHES DGOS SO,,
32983.wylie: yang de nyid las, lugs dam pa 'dis ni yan lag tshogs pa tsam dang de'i ya gyal sogs gang yang yan lag can la sogs pa'i mtshan gzhir mi rung yang, yan lag can la sogs pa ming du btags pa tsam la bya byed legs par 'jog nus pa gsung rab kyi don du 'grel ba thub pa'i dgongs pa thun mong ma yin pa yin pas dgongs pa 'grel lugs 'di la sbyang bar bya'o, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar yin pas shes dgos so
32983.english: That said, one really should try to grasp the import of the following words from the same work, as they describe how these things really are: This highest of all the systems would say that the collection of the parts in itself—and the individual parts and so on—cannot be pointed to as a definitive instance of the thing composed of those parts, or anything of the like. Nonetheless, if we consider things like the whole made of the parts, as these are simply imputed in name, we are able to establish, perfectly, the way in which things do things. When we explain the meaning of the high words of the Buddha in this way, we have come to the truly unique thought of these teachings. As such, I encourage you to verse yourselves in this manner of interpreting the true intent of the Enlightened One.

33056.acip: RJE'I 'JUG tIK LAS, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYI DGONGS PA SHIN TU PHRA BA'I GNAS RNAMS RJEN CHER DU STON PA'I MKHAS PA'I DBANG PO'I BZHED PA THUN MONG MA YIN PA 'DI RNAMS LEGS PAR SHES PA LA 'BAD PAR GYIS SHIG ,CES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
33056.wylie: rje'i 'jug Tik las, bcom ldan 'das kyi dgongs pa shin tu phra ba'i gnas rnams rjen cher du ston pa'i mkhas pa'i dbang po'i bzhed pa thun mong ma yin pa 'di rnams legs par shes pa la 'bad par gyis shig ,ces gsungs pa'i phyir ro
33056.english: And that, in turn, is true because of the following statement that we find in the Lord's commentary upon Entering the Middle Way: These are the unique positions taken by the Lords of the Wise, where they lay completely bare the very most subtle points within the true intent of the Conquering Buddhas. Make intense efforts then to learn them well. Specific proofs for establishing that no things are themselves

33078.acip: GRANGS CAN GYIS SPYIR SKYE BA ZHIG YIN NA, YOD DGOS PAS MYU GU YANG RANG GI RGYU DUS SU MED NA MI SKYE BAS DE'I DUS SU MI GSAL BA'I TSUL GYIS YOD PA NYID, SLAR GSAL BAR SKYE BAS BDAG SKYE YOD DO, ,ZHES 'DOD,
33078.wylie: grangs can gyis spyir skye ba zhig yin na, yod dgos pas myu gu yang rang gi rgyu dus su med na mi skye bas de'i dus su mi gsal ba'i tshul gyis yod pa nyid, slar gsal bar skye bas bdag skye yod do, ,zhes 'dod
33078.english: The Numerist School would say the following: There really do exist cases where things start from themselves. If something is starting, then it must indeed exist; and so if a sprout were not somehow present during the period of its cause, it could never start. As such, we accept the idea of a sprout which is present at that time, but in a way where it is not yet distinct. And then that indistinct starting reaches a point where it starts further—now in a distinct way.

33098.acip: GZHAN YANG, RMA BYA'I MDONGS DE RANG GI RGYU LAS SKYES PAR THAL, DE RMA BYA'I THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I LAS DANG RANG GI NYER LEN SNGA MA LAS SKYES PA'I PHYIR,
33098.wylie: gzhan yang, rma bya'i mdongs de rang gi rgyu las skyes par thal, de rma bya'i thun mong ma yin pa'i las dang rang gi nyer len snga ma las skyes pa'i phyir
33098.english: Or we could argue it like this: Isn't it, indeed, the case that the colored spot in the design of a peacock's feather is something that starts from its own particular cause? Why do you say that? Because isn't that spot something that grows due to the peacock's own unique karma; and from its own unique material cause, which is something that came before it?

33114.acip: RTEN 'BREL LA THUN MONG BA DANG THUN MONG MA YIN PA GNYIS LAS,
33114.wylie: rten 'brel la thun mong ba dang thun mong ma yin pa gnyis las
33114.english: The concept of interdependence can be described in two different ways: there is the common explanation, and then the uncommon explanation.

33116.acip: THUN MONG MA YIN PA NI, THAL 'GYUR BA'I LUGS KYI RTOG PAS BTAGS TZAM DU GRUB PA'I TSUL SHES DGOS TE, SNGAR GYI RIGS PA DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG MTHAR GTUGS NA RTEN 'BREL GYI RIGS PA LA THUG PAS SO,,
33116.wylie: thun mong ma yin pa ni, thal 'gyur ba'i lugs kyi rtog pas btags tsam du grub pa'i tshul shes dgos te, sngar gyi rigs pa de dag thams cad kyang mthar gtugs na rten 'brel gyi rigs pa la thug pas so
33116.english: As for the uncommon explanation, you will need to understand the presentation of the Consequence branch on how things exist as no more than projections of our conceptions. We can in fact say that the preceding proofs we've presented all come down to this one: to the proof based on interdependence.

33678.acip: YANG GANG ZAG 'GA' ZHIG LA DMIGS RTEN GZUGS CAN LAS GZUGS MED 'CHAR BDE BA 'BYUNG BAS, DE 'DRA DAG GIS NI, RJE'I LAM RIM CHUNG NGU'I DGONGS PA PAn CHEN CHOS RGYAN GYIS SROL PHYES PA
33678.wylie: yang gang zag 'ga' zhig la dmigs rten gzugs can las gzugs med 'char bde ba 'byung bas, de 'dra dag gis ni, rje'i lam rim chung ngu'i dgongs pa paN chen chos rgyan gyis srol phyes pa
33678.english: There are certain kinds of practitioners, on the other hand, who find it easier to choose a meditation object which is more ineffable—not so concrete. If you're someone like this, then you might prefer the system that His Holiness the First Panchen Lama—Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen—developed based on the train of thought found in Je Tsongkapa's briefer presentation on the steps of the path.

33904.acip: DANG PO LA THUN MONG DANG THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I GLENG GZHI GNYIS YOD PA'I DANG PO LA BZHI STE, DUS DANG STON PA DANG GNAS DANG 'KHOR PHUN SUM TSOGS PA BZHI'O,,

34916.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

34917.english: Our second point [that you have failed to comprehend the position we expressed above] is also quite true. Our original position was describing a situation where three different kinds of beings were sitting together and looking at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It is not our position that the glass full of something wet and flowing is one thing that is three different things. And it is not our position that there is such a thing as the physical appearance of a person which is at once both attractive and ugly. It is furthermore not our position that the blood and pus represent some kind of physical form which results from karma and grows up between the visual consciousness of the craving spirit and the stream of water. And it is not our position that the craving spirit's eyes see both this blood and pus as some kind of physical form resulting from karma, and the river of water at the same time. It is our position that, by force of his karma, the craving spirit is not able to see the stream of water.
